item.title: Readout 0.3.0
item.description:
• Quit your own apps and processes from the top lists. Hover over a row and click ✕, or right-click it, then confirm in the box that opens below the row. Quit works like ⌘Q, so apps with unsaved work ask first. If an app hasn't quit after 5 seconds, you can force quit it from the same box.
  • The right-click menu also offers Force Quit, Show in Finder, and Copy PID.
  • System processes can't be quit, and neither can Readout itself or loginwindow (quitting it would log you out).
  • Fixed: in English, the memory list's subtitle no longer gets cut off.

item.title: Readout 0.2.1
item.description:
• A "Hide system" checkbox below each top list, on by default, hides processes owned by other users. Uncheck it to include them. Your choice is remembered.
  • Fixed: with system processes included, the memory list now shows their real memory use (for example, WindowServer), matching Activity Monitor.
  • The power list always excludes system processes, because macOS does not report their energy use.

item.title: Readout 0.2.0
item.description:
• Click the CPU, memory, network, or power tile to see the top 10 apps or processes using it (up to 20). Switch between apps, with helper processes combined into their app, and individual processes. Processes owned by other users are marked System. Press ‹ or Esc to go back.
  • The lists refresh every 3 seconds only while they are on screen, and stop when you go back or close the panel.
  • The power list ranks apps by CPU energy. macOS does not report energy for other users' processes, so they are not included there.

item.title: Readout 0.1.2
item.description:
• The menu bar is more compact in metrics mode: tighter spacing between metrics and smaller unit labels (%, W, K, M), so four metrics now take about 205 points instead of 228.
  • Network rates always fit in three digits: a value that rounds up to 1000K is now shown as 1.0M.

item.title: Readout 0.1.1
item.description:
• The panel fills in faster: CPU and network now appear in about 0.2 seconds (was about 0.5), and disks are read about five times faster.
  • Readout now also pauses its background readings while another user is logged in (fast user switching), in addition to sleep and display sleep.

item.title: Readout 0.1.0
item.description:
• First release.
  • Menu bar icon with a panel showing CPU, memory, network, power, and every mounted disk with its free space.
  • Metrics mode: show CPU, memory, network, and power directly in the menu bar, in the order you choose.
  • Refresh interval from 30 seconds to 15 minutes; nothing is read in the background in icon-only mode.
  • Automatic update checks (once a day) with Sparkle; check manually from the right-click menu or Settings.
  • Korean and English (choose in Settings).
